title: Decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification for quantum low-density parity-check codes
authors: Josu Etxezarreta Martinez, Francisco Garcia-Herrero, Ruben M. Otxoa, Reza Dastbasteh
abstract: Real-time decoding is a fundamental necessity for building fault-tolerant quantum computers. In this work, we introduce decoding with alternating weighted graph sparsification (DAWG), an ensemble based approach that combines Tanner graph sparsification with ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders. The DAWG decoder runs BP decoders over the full detector error model Tanner graph for certain iterations to then transfer the posteriors to a sparsified graph in which additional rounds of BP are run. Each of the decoders in the ensemble uses a different transfer matrix to map the posterior information to the sparsified graph. We use the serial schedule for the minimum-sum BP decoders and, thus, employ Vibe decoding ideas by randomizing the schedules of each of them. The performance of the DAWG decoder is then numerically studied for bivariate bicycle codes and superdense color code circuits to be compared with other state-of-the-art decoding approaches. Importantly, the DAWG decoder shows a similar performance to Relay belief-propagation and Vibe decoding when combined with an order-$0$ Localized Statistics Decoding (LSD-$0$) post-processor. Crucially, the post-processor is called an order of magnitude less times than for Vibe with the same ensemble size, indicating that the introduced latency tail will be minimal. Furthermore, LSD-$0$ operates on a sparsified decoding graph of a fraction of the size of the full detector error model, which simplifies the resources required by specialized hardware to support it. Overall, the DAWG+LSD-$0$ decoder represents a viable low-cost BP-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes.
summary: This paper introduces DAWG, a novel, ensemble-based decoding algorithm for quantum error correction codes. It improves upon existing methods by alternating between decoding on a full graph and a significantly sparser graph using weighted sparsification. The resulting DAWG+LSD-0 decoder is shown to be highly competitive with minimal overhead, suggesting a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_problem: The primary goal is achieving real-time, fault-tolerant decoding for quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes, which is crucial for building functional quantum computers.
main_result: The proposed DAWG+LSD-0 decoder demonstrates performance matching state-of-the-art methods like RelayBP, while significantly reducing the required frequency of the post-processor, making it a low-cost, viable algorithm.
method: The approach, Decoding with Alternating Weighted Graph Sparsification (DAWG), combines ensembling belief-propagation (BP) decoders with Tanner graph sparsification, using different transfer matrices to enrich soft information.
model_or_system: The work models quantum error correction using qLDPC codes defined over a Detector Error Model (DEM) graph. The core technique involves relating the full DEM to a much sparser version using a transfer matrix.
key_observables: Logical error rates, latency, and hardware resource requirements are the key performance metrics used for comparison.
important_parameters: The sparsification process reduces the variable nodes in the graph to a fraction (e.g., 25%) of the original size, simplifying hardware implementation.
main_assumptions: The method assumes the ability to construct an ensemble using diverse transfer matrices and relies on the performance of the LSD-0 post-processor for non-converged decoding rounds.
figures_summary: Figures compare the logical error rate performance of DAWG+LSD-0 against other decoders (like Vibe and BP+LSD-0) across various qLDPC codes (e.g., BB codes, Gross code).
paper_structure: The paper introduces the DAWG decoder, details its multi-stage process (full graph BP -> sparsification/transfer -> sparsified graph BP -> post-processing), and then numerically compares its performance against established state-of-the-art decoding techniques.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum error correction, the underlying mathematical structure involving graph sparsification, ensemble averaging, and iterative belief propagation shares conceptual links with advanced classical simulation techniques used in condensed matter physics.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The DAWG+LSD-0 decoder. The decoder operates three stages: a) Ensemble of randomized serial BP runs over the full DEM, b) Ensemble of randomized serial BP runs over the sparsified DEM with propagated LLRs using different transfer matrices and c) LSD-0 with normalized sum of posterior LLRs from the sparsified DEM runs. Each of the stages is called if the previous ones did not converge. Upon convergence, the most likely error across the ensemble is chosen as a solution based on the prior probabilties.

Figure 2: Performance of DAWG for BB codes. a) [[72, 12, 6]]. b) [[108, 8, 10]]. c) [[144, 12, 12]]. The shading highlights the region of estimated probabilities where the likelihood ratio is within a factor of 1000.

Figure 3: Probability that DAWG and Vibe do not converge per round for the Gross code. DAWG shows much rarer unconvergence than Vibe, with the difference being accentuated when the physical error rate lowers.
